entities.name: TMS-protected alkyne
observations: Structure decodes as CC(O)(C#C[Si](C)(C)C)c1ccc(F)cn1; the ethynyl group is protected as a trimethylsilyl alkyne.
The queried transformation removes the trimethylsilyl group to form a terminal alkyne without changing the tertiary propargylic alcohol or fluoropyridyl ring.

entities.name: Terminal alkynyl pyridyl alcohol
observations: Product structure is C#CC(C)(O)c1ccc(F)cn1, corresponding to TMS deprotection of the protected ethynyl precursor.
The transformation is consistent with Si–C bond cleavage rather than rearrangement or cross-coupling.

entities.name: TMS alkyne desilylation
observations: Closest ORD analog ord-aa0eb5df16264d5db4862e46b8e4ea23 uses potassium fluoride and gives the terminal alkyne in 86% yield; methanol and ethyl acetate are listed as solvents.
A second fluoride-containing ORD record is a weaker analog because it includes additional coupling or organometallic components.

entities.name: Potassium fluoride desilylation
observations: Potassium fluoride ([K+][F−]) is the closest supported reagent for removing the trimethylsilyl group from the queried alkyne.
Methanol and ethyl acetate were listed in the closest ORD precedent; the reported isolated yield was 86%.
